# flightdeck_service_account_api_token (Resource)

Manages a REST API token (`fd_pat_…`) of a Flightdeck service account: the credential an application uses to call Flightdeck's API as that account. The token can do whatever the account can, so give the account only the project access the application needs.

**Every read and write needs a token whose user is a workspace owner or admin.**

The token value is returned by the API **once, on create**, and stored in Terraform state as a sensitive attribute so it can be handed to the application (for example through a secret manager). It is never re-read; an imported token has no `token` value. Tokens can't be edited: changing any argument replaces the token.

**For rotation, set `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }`.** By default Terraform deletes the old token before it makes the new one, so the application is cut off until it gets the new value. With `create_before_destroy`, Terraform makes the new token first, updates whatever uses its value (such as a secret that holds it), and deletes the old token last.

`expires_at` is an RFC 3339 time with a time zone, such as `2027-06-01T00:00:00Z`. Leave it out for a token that never expires. Flightdeck answers with the same time in its own zone, and the provider compares the two as times and keeps what the configuration says. A time that has passed fails the plan of a new token, because Flightdeck won't make a token that is already expired. When a token in state has expired, the plan warns: set a later `expires_at` to replace it. The provider can't replace it on its own, since the new token would get the same time that has passed.

A create is made idempotent with a key derived from `service_account_id`, `name` and `expires_at`, and Flightdeck keeps those keys per provider token, so two tokens declared for one service account with all three the same, and made with the same provider token, are one create as far as the API is concerned, for the 24 hours it remembers a create. While the first token is live, Flightdeck refuses the second create rather than replay it without its secret, and the apply fails naming the token that already exists: change `name` or `expires_at` on the resource the error is reported on. The same error follows an apply that failed after Flightdeck made the token; then delete the token it names and apply again. A replacement that destroys first is not affected (the old token is gone by then), but one under `create_before_destroy` with the same values (`terraform apply -replace`), within 24 hours of the old token's create, is refused the same way. A rotation changes `expires_at` or `name`, so it is not affected.

Deleting the resource deletes the token, and it stops working at once. Removing the service account from the workspace deletes its tokens too, and a token whose account is gone leaves state on the next refresh.

Import with `<service_account_id>/<token_id>`: `terraform import flightdeck_service_account_api_token.deploy 980190966/2129`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "flightdeck_service_account" "deploy" {
  email_address = "deploy-bot@machineusers.example.com"
  name          = "Deploy Bot"
}

resource "flightdeck_service_account_api_token" "deploy" {
  service_account_id = flightdeck_service_account.deploy.id
  name               = "Deploy production"
  # Leave expires_at out for a token that never expires. To rotate the
  # token, set a later time: that replaces it.
  expires_at = "2027-06-01T00:00:00Z"

  # Make the new token before deleting the old one, so the application is
  # not cut off while it waits for the new value.
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

# The token value is only returned on create; hand it to the application
# through a secret store rather than an output.
# output "deploy_token" {
#   value     = flightdeck_service_account_api_token.deploy.token
#   sensitive = true
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Label shown in the service account's token list, at most 255 characters (for example the application's name and environment). Changing it replaces the token.
- `service_account_id` (Number) Id of the service account the token belongs to (`flightdeck_service_account.id`). Changing it replaces the token.

### Optional

- `expires_at` (String) When the token stops working: an RFC 3339 time with a time zone, such as `2027-06-01T00:00:00Z`. Leave it out for a token that never expires. It must be in the future when the token is made. The same time written another way, for example in another time zone, is not a change. Changing it to another time replaces the token.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the token was made (RFC 3339, in the server's time zone).
- `id` (Number) Numeric id of the token.
- `last_four` (String) Last four characters of the token.
- `masked` (String) The token with all but its last four characters hidden, as the token list shows it.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The token value (`fd_pat_…`). Available only when the resource created the token.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with "<service_account_id>/<token_id>". An imported token has no
# `token` value, and an expired token cannot be imported.
terraform import flightdeck_service_account_api_token.deploy 980190966/2129
```
